overview: A layered FastAPI application: an HTTP layer that only translates requests and errors, a service layer that owns the business rules, and a repository that owns all SQL against an embedded SQLite database. The application is built by a factory so tests and deployments inject their own settings.

New table recording applied migration versions

decisions.title: FastAPI on SQLite behind a repository seam
decisions.context: The prototype must run with one command and no infrastructure, yet must not lock the design into an embedded database.
decisions.decision: Use FastAPI with the standard-library sqlite3 driver. Only repository.py and db.py know SQL.
alternatives: PostgreSQL from day one (needs infrastructure to run the prototype)
An ORM (more dependencies and indirection than six queries justify)
decisions.consequences: Zero-setup local runs and tests; moving to a client/server database replaces two modules. Write throughput is limited to one writer.

decisions.title: Random base62 codes with database-enforced uniqueness
decisions.context: Codes must be short, unique and not enumerable.
decisions.decision: Generate 7 random base62 characters from the OS CSPRNG; rely on the primary key for uniqueness and retry a collision up to 5 times.
alternatives: Encode an auto-increment id (enumerable, reveals volume)
Hash of the URL (forces deduplication, collisions on truncation)
decisions.consequences: No coordination between instances is needed. Collision probability stays negligible until billions of links; exhaustion surfaces as a retryable 503.

decisions.title: 307 redirects that are never cached
decisions.context: Analytics are only correct if every visit reaches the service.
decisions.decision: Answer GET /{code} with 307 and Cache-Control: no-store.
alternatives: 301 permanent redirect (cached by browsers, undercounts clicks and makes deletion ineffective)
decisions.consequences: Accurate counts and immediate effect of deletion, at the cost of one extra round trip per visit.

decisions.title: Soft delete
decisions.context: Removing a link must stop redirects without destroying its history.
decisions.decision: DELETE marks the link inactive; redirects then answer 410 Gone.
alternatives: Hard delete (loses analytics, lets a code be reissued to a different destination)
decisions.consequences: Codes are never reused, which prevents old links from silently pointing somewhere new.

decisions.title: Forward-only migrations applied at start-up
decisions.context: The schema must be reproducible and evolvable by later changes.
decisions.decision: Keep an ordered list of migrations; apply the pending ones transactionally on start and record them in schema_migrations.
alternatives: A migration framework (unneeded dependency for a single-file schema)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (cannot express later changes)
decisions.consequences: A new instance and an upgraded instance converge on the same schema. Rolling back a release requires migrations to be backward compatible.

risks.description: SQLite allows a single writer; redirect bursts queue behind click inserts.
risks.mitigation: WAL mode and a busy timeout; the repository seam allows moving to a server database or buffering clicks.

risks.description: The service can be used to disguise malicious destinations (open redirect by design).
risks.mitigation: Only http(s) URLs are accepted in v1; destination vetting and rate limiting are explicitly out of scope and tracked as follow-up.

risks.description: The clicks table grows without bound.
risks.mitigation: Indexed by (code, clicked_at); the stats window is bounded. Retention or roll-ups are a follow-up.

risks.description: Unauthenticated API allows anyone to create or delete links.
risks.mitigation: Assumption A1: deployed behind a trusted gateway. Authentication is out of scope for v1.

requirement_coverage.approach: POST /api/v1/links -> LinkService.create validates the URL and allocates a code with bounded retry
GET /{code} -> LinkService.resolve returns the destination; the route answers 307
DELETE /api/v1/links/{code} -> soft delete; resolve raises LinkGone -> 410
resolve records a click row; GET .../stats aggregates count, last click and per-day totals
/healthz and /readyz, durable SQLite file in WAL mode, transactional writes, global error handlers
Bound parameters only, URL and code validation, bounded referrer and request-id
Request-id middleware and an access log line per request
Three layers with one-way dependencies, env-driven Settings, unit and API tests, generated OpenAPI

rollback_plan: Greenfield: nothing exists to regress. The change is only promoted to the target directory after release approval, and `sdlc rollback` removes the promoted files again.
limitations: Single-writer SQLite: suitable for a prototype or a single instance, not for horizontal scaling
No authentication, rate limiting or destination vetting in v1
Analytics are computed on read; no retention policy for click rows
